findings.title: Small-action button no longer pins to the right
findings.body: .small-action is now a flex container (display:flex plus the prefixed flexbox mixin), so the button's float:right is ignored in every browser that takes that display. The button is only a flex item with the default flex: 0 1 auto and no margin-left: auto, so it sits immediately after .small-action-desc instead of at the far edge of the row. The same change also drops the 4em left padding that used to clear the floated avatar; in browsers that do not apply flex, the avatar's float:left then overlaps the description.

findings.title: Header panel alignment breaks under the prefixed flexbox the mixin enables
findings.body: .panel lost float:right and now relies on margin-left:auto while .contents is turned into a flex container by the new flexbox() mixin, which emits display:-ms-flexbox and display:-webkit-box before display:flex. Those older flex models do not absorb auto margins, and once they apply, floats on flex items are ignored. In IE10 (and old WebKit that only honors the 2009 box syntax) the panel therefore stays next to the title instead of on the right. There is no float or justify-content fallback left in the rule.

findings.title: order() mixin uses 0-based values for 1-based box-ordinal-group
findings.body: The 2009 flexbox properties -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group are 1-based (the initial value is 1) and reject 0, while modern order and -ms-flex-order are 0-based. The mixin writes the same $val to all of them. order(1) therefore sorts with default siblings in old WebKit instead of after them, and order(0) is invalid there. Header and topic styles already call order(2) and order(3); those two happen to stay after default items, but any later order(0) or order(1) will not match modern layout in the browsers this mixin claims to prefix.

findings.title: extra-info-wrapper order has no flex parent
findings.body: order(2) is set on .extra-info-wrapper and order(3) on .d-header .panel, but this change only makes .d-header .contents a flex container. .extra-info-wrapper is not a descendant of .contents in these styles, so it is not a flex item and order does nothing. The docked topic title will not slot between the site title and the header panel the way the order values imply; only in-flow children of .contents participate.
